- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.0), model often overcorrects upward; cap forecast growth to prevent excessive lagged momentum.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; adjust upward slightly to account for mean reversion.
- Model frequently underestimates true outcomes in early forecast windows (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; apply slight upward bias for short-term horizon.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or low values, model tends to ignore downward momentum; increase downward bias to reflect suppressed sentiment.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture true mean reversion; apply a smoothing filter to align with recent 7–14 day average if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
